Water Line Replacement Cost in Sarasota: What to Expect

By SRQ Leak Pros Editorial · Published November 4, 2026 · Updated November 7, 2026 · 5 min read

Short answer: Angi reports a national average water line replacement cost of about $1,710, with most homeowners paying $647 to $2,828, or about $50 to $250 per linear foot. A Sarasota quote can be higher or lower depending on line length, depth, trench or trenchless method, driveways in the path, permits and restoration.

Replacing a main water line is one of the bigger plumbing bills a homeowner faces, so it helps to know what drives the price before you get quotes. Costs vary a lot from yard to yard. If your line keeps leaking, SRQ Leak Pros can connect you with a local pro for water line replacement in Sarasota and a written estimate.

The figures below are national data from one named source, not a Sarasota price list. Your quote depends on your property.

What does water line replacement cost?

Angi's cost guide for main water line replacement, updated December 2, 2024, reports:

MeasureAngi national figure
Average total costAbout $1,710
Typical rangeAbout $647 to $2,828
Cost per linear footAbout $50 to $250

These are national averages. They don't include every situation, such as long runs under driveways or pools.

What changes the cost of a water line replacement?

Seven factors do most of the work.

  1. Length. Price often scales with feet of pipe. Deep, platted lots with homes set far back have longer lines.
  2. Depth. Deeper lines need more digging or longer bores.
  3. Method. An open trench is often simplest in open lawn. Trenchless pipe bursting or boring costs more per foot but can save on restoration.
  4. Obstacles. Driveways, pavers, pools, trees and irrigation in the path add time or force a trenchless method.
  5. Pipe material and size. PEX, HDPE and copper differ in cost. A larger diameter line costs more.
  6. Permits and inspection. Most jurisdictions require a permit for a line replacement.
  7. Restoration. Replacing sod, concrete, pavers and sprinkler heads can add a lot.

Trench vs. trenchless: how the cost compares

Trenchless isn't always cheaper or more expensive. It shifts the cost from restoration to equipment.

MethodCost patternBest value when
Open trenchLower equipment cost, higher restoration costOpen lawn with little hardscape
Pipe burstingHigher equipment cost, small pits onlyThe old line runs straight and can be split
Directional boringHigher equipment cost, small pits onlyDriveways, pools or trees sit over the line

Wikipedia describes pipe bursting as replacing buried pipe without a traditional trench, using launching and receiving pits. Read the trenchless water line replacement guide for the methods in detail.

Hidden costs to ask about

  • Locating the old line. If no one knows where it runs, locating time adds up.
  • A new main shut-off valve. Often worth adding if the old one is stuck.
  • A pressure reducing valve. If incoming pressure is high, it protects the new line.
  • Irrigation repair. Sprinkler lines often cross the service line.
  • Disposal or abandonment of the old pipe.
  • After-hours work if the line has failed suddenly.

How to compare quotes

Get at least two written estimates and make sure they cover the same work.

  • The method (trench, burst, bore) and why
  • Pipe material, diameter and length
  • Permit and inspection included
  • 811 locate ticket included
  • New shut-off valve or pressure reducing valve
  • Surface restoration: what is restored and what isn't
  • Cleanup and old pipe removal
  • The provider's Florida license number

Check the license on the state DBPR license search. Florida law places water line installation within the plumbing contractor's scope.

Does insurance pay for water line replacement?

Usually not for a worn-out pipe. Many homeowners policies exclude wear and tear. Some cover sudden damage caused by a break, and some insurers sell service line coverage. If you plan to file a claim for damage, Florida Statutes § 627.70132 requires notice within 1 year after the date of loss. Talk with your agent. This is general information, not insurance advice.

Repair or replace: a cost decision

A single break in a sound line is often cheaper to repair. Replacement wins when:

  • The line has leaked more than once
  • It is polybutylene or galvanized steel
  • Pressure is low because the pipe is narrowed inside
  • You're about to pour a driveway or build a pool over it

How to keep replacement costs down

  • Find and mark the meter, shut-off and line entry before the visit.
  • Clear plants and objects from the work path.
  • Ask whether trenchless saves on restoration in your yard.
  • Bundle the job with other planned yard work.
  • Replace on your schedule, before an emergency.

Local note: long lines on deep lots in North Port push replacement costs up, so trenchless options are worth pricing. In Lakewood Ranch, landscaping and irrigation over the line make restoration a big part of the bill. Older lines in Bradenton are often galvanized and due for full replacement.

Related reading: before you price a new line, learn who is responsible for the water line from the street to the house. If the inside plumbing is old too, see polybutylene pipes in Florida. If one fix may do, compare the cost to repair a main water line, and check typical water line burial depth before you dig.

When should you call a water line professional?

Call a pro for a quote when:

  • Your line has leaked more than once
  • You have polybutylene or galvanized pipe
  • Pressure has dropped and won't come back
  • You're planning hardscape or a pool over the line

Frequently asked questions

How much does it cost to replace a water line per foot?

Angi's national data puts it at about $50 to $250 per linear foot. Your price depends on depth, method, material and restoration.

Is trenchless water line replacement more expensive?

It can cost more per foot, but it often saves money on concrete, paver and landscape repair. Compare the full cost of each option.

Does a permit add much to the cost?

Permit fees vary by jurisdiction. Ask whether the permit and inspection are included in the quote.

Can I replace just part of my water line?

Yes, a damaged section can be replaced. If the rest of the pipe is old or failing, a full replacement may cost less over time.
